program:
chomsky: grammars as data, one at each level of Chomsky's hierarchy, each classed and its words listed. Deciding a word is total up to the context-sensitive level, where no rule shrinks a form; at the unrestricted level the search has no bound (Diverge) and runs under with fuel.
Prior art: the hierarchy, Noam Chomsky, "Three models for the description of language" (1956) and "On certain formal properties of grammars" (1959); context-sensitive languages decided in bounded space, S.-Y. Kuroda, "Classes of languages and linear-bounded automata" (1964).
Adapted: the grammar of a's in powers of two is the example in John Hopcroft and Jeffrey Ullman, Introduction to Automata Theory, Languages, and Computation (1979).
Influence: JFLAP (Susan H. Rodger, Duke University), grammars and machines as objects to convert and test against each other.
